claims.claim: Kay says a major novel can be made to sound trivial, silly or shallow if boiled down to a paragraph of sound bite.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'The Big Idea: Guy Gavriel Kay', Whatever (John Scalzi's blog), 2025
claims.quote: can be made to sound trivial, silly, shallow if boiled down
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Of course you don't'

claims.claim: Pembroke College reports that Kay's Tolkien Lecture discussed the vital importance of the unsaid and the unexplained in fiction.
claims.source: Pembroke College, Oxford (report of Kay's Tolkien Lecture 'Just Enough Light'), 2021
claims.quote: the vital importance of the unsaid and the unexplained in fiction

claims.claim: Kay asked in the lecture how comfortable we are in our responses to art with mystery and with not knowing.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, quoted from the 2021 Tolkien Lecture in Pembroke College's report, 2021
claims.quote: how comfortable in our responses to art are we with mystery
claims.page: news item, second paragraph (quotation from the lecture)

claims.claim: Kay's hundred-word Sarantine Mosaic Drabble opens with a ten-word sentence.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'Aliana in the West' (a 100-word Drabble, (c)2014), reproduced at Bright Weavings, 2025
claims.quote: She is lying beside her love dreaming of her love.

claims.claim: Bright Weavings records that Kay wrote two Drabbles in 2014, a Drabble being a 100 word short story.
claims.source: Bright Weavings (Alec Lynch), editorial note on Kay's Drabbles, 2025
claims.quote: A Drabble is a 100 word short story

claims.claim: That opening sentence of Kay's Drabble repeats the phrase 'her love' twice.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'Aliana in the West' (a 100-word Drabble, (c)2014), reproduced at Bright Weavings, 2025
claims.quote: She is lying beside her love dreaming of her love.

claims.claim: Wolfe says Kay deploys an impressive variety of narrative voices in All the Seas of the World.
claims.source: Gary K. Wolfe, review of All the Seas of the World, Locus (May 2022 issue; posted 2022-06-25)
claims.quote: Kay deploys an impressive variety of such narrative voices

claims.claim: Wolfe says the occasional shift into first person has something of the effect of hearing a skilled soloist in a symphony.
claims.source: Gary K. Wolfe, review of All the Seas of the World, Locus (May 2022 issue; posted 2022-06-25)
claims.quote: the occasional shift into first-person has something of the effect

claims.claim: Wolfe says Kay's devoted readers have come to learn his invented nomenclature for nations, cities and geographical features.
claims.source: Gary K. Wolfe, review of All the Seas of the World, Locus (May 2022 issue; posted 2022-06-25)
claims.quote: his invented nomenclature for nations, cities, geographical features

claims.claim: Wolfe says that despite an intimidating character list at the front, the on-the-ground tale is a model of clarity and focus.
claims.source: Gary K. Wolfe, review of All the Seas of the World, Locus (May 2022 issue; posted 2022-06-25)
claims.quote: the on-the-ground tale is a model of clarity and focus

claims.claim: Wolfe says even secondary figures gain a haunting presence when the reader is offered brief glimpses into their future lives.
claims.source: Gary K. Wolfe, review of All the Seas of the World, Locus (May 2022 issue; posted 2022-06-25)
claims.quote: brief glimpses into their future lives
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'As his isolated and exiled figures'

claims.claim: Wolfe says the novel reminds the reader more than once that lives pivot on small things and accidents of timing.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay's novel All the Seas of the World, quoted by Gary K. Wolfe in Locus, 2022
claims.quote: Lives change, turn, pivot on small things, accidents of timing
